(Muktau)ānandatāratamyakhaṇḍana
viś. adv. by Aṇṇayārya II of Tirumala Bukkapaṭṭaṇam family. Adyar II. p. 155b. IO. 6023. MT. 1294.

(Muni)devasūri
descendant of Vādi Devasūri, an. pupil of Madanacandrasūri.
--Śāntināthacaritra in 7 chs. composed in Sam3. 1338. based on Devacandra's Pkt. work, an. corrected by Pradyumna, pupil of Kanakaprabha an. grand pupil of Devānanda. IO. 7668. Peters. I. App. p. 4.

(Muḍumbai)narasiṃhācārya
called Saṅgīta Muḍumbai; of Śrīvatsagotra.
--Bharatasarvārthasaṅgraha or Bharatārṇava. MT. 2435.

(Muḍumbai)narasiṃhācārya
(1842-1928 A. D.) called Sāhitya Muḍumbai; prolific writer in Sanskrit an. Telugu.
--Rāmacandrakathāmṛta. [Page366-a.
--C. Sāṅkhyataruvasanta on Sāṅkhyasaptati of Īśvarakṛṣṇa. in a theistic manner. Adyar D. VIII. 10. Extr. p. 289.
--C. Vyākhyā on Sāṅkhyparavacanasūtra. ibid. 13. Extr. p.. 289-90.
For the other works attributed to him see intro. to Rāmacandrakathāmṛta (Pt.. Fort Vizianagar, 1915.) also P. K. Sasidharan Nair, Annals of Ori. Res. XXVI.

(Muḍumba)nṛsiṃhācārya
of Śrīvatsagotra; of Saṅgīta Muḍumbai family.
--Bharatasarvārthasaṅgraha. MT. 1668.

(muni)padmanandin
Jain.
-- Jinarātrīvratamāhātmya. 1480 A. D.
See K. C. Jain, Jainism in Rajasthan p. 194.

(mūla)mantrārthakārikā(mālikā)
or Aṣṭākṣarārthakārikā or Rahasyatrayakārikā (viś. adv.) by Nārāyaṇa of Cintāpattana family. The a. salutes Vīrarāghavācārya, son of Raghunāthācārya of Kandāḍai (Kūrakula) family. Adyar I. p. 188a. Adyar D. X. 405. Extr. p. 359. MD. 17153. MT. 160 (n). 3123. 4772.
